# CANDIDATE: NAMED_LEVEL_DOUBLE_TOUCH_LONG

**Filed:** 2026-07-09  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

A second test of a named level (prior day high, prior day low, or daily pivot) with increasing volume on the second touch and bullish EMA ribbon alignment (EMA9 > EMA20 > EMA50) often produces a bounce long entry. This edge exists because named levels act as short-term support/resistance, and a retest with rising volume and aligned momentum suggests institutional interest in holding the level, increasing probability of a mean-reversion bounce.

## Mechanism

Entry: Price approaches a named level (prior day high, prior day low, or daily pivot) within 0.1% and makes two touches within three 5-minute bars. The second touch must show higher volume than the first touch AND have EMA9 > EMA20 > EMA50 on the second touch bar. Enter long at the close of the second touch bar.  
Exit: Stop placed below the low of the second touch bar. Target is the next named level above (e.g., if testing prior day low, target prior day high) or at 1.5R, whichever is closer.  
Regime filters: Only consider entries between 11:00-14:00 ET and when VIX < 20. Avoid entries during high-impact news or opening-range volatility spikes (first 30 minutes after open).
